---
title: "Activation Reload/Restart Deprecation"
---

# Activation Reload/Restart Deprecation

NixOS 26.05 deprecated **reloading or restarting systemd units from the NixOS activation script**, with removal targeted for **26.11**. The boring default is: **stop writing unit names into `/run/nixos/activation-restart-list` or `/run/nixos/activation-reload-list` from `system.activationScripts`; declare restart/reload behavior on the unit itself (`restartTriggers`, `reloadIfChanged`, `restartIfChanged`), and migrate other activation work to `systemd.tmpfiles.settings`, `ExecStartPre=`, or a oneshot service ordered with `sysinit-reactivation.target`.**

Activation scripts used to be the catch-all "run shell after every switch." That model serializes boot, fights parallelism, and is on a multi-release path toward removal (see the nixpkgs tracking effort). The 26.05 release notes call out the reload/restart side channel first because nixpkgs itself no longer uses it. Desk configs that still poke those list files will keep working through 26.05 with deprecation pressure, then break on 26.11.

## Mental model

```
nixos-rebuild switch / boot
        │
        ▼
 activation script fragments     ← system.activationScripts.*
   (legacy: echo unit >> /run/nixos/activation-restart-list)
        │
        ▼
 switch-to-configuration
   reads restart/reload lists    ← DEPRECATED path (gone in 26.11)
   OR applies unit metadata      ← preferred: restartTriggers / reloadIfChanged
        │
        ▼
 systemd starts / reloads / restarts units
```

| Piece | Role |
|---|---|
| `system.activationScripts` | Shell fragments run on activate (boot + switch); being phased out over several releases |
| `/run/nixos/activation-restart-list` | Legacy side channel: activation script asks STC to restart units |
| `/run/nixos/activation-reload-list` | Legacy side channel: activation script asks STC to reload units |
| `systemd.services.<name>.restartTriggers` | Declared restart when listed store paths / strings change |
| `systemd.services.<name>.reloadIfChanged` | Prefer reload over restart when the unit file changes |
| `systemd.services.<name>.restartIfChanged` | Default-ish restart policy for unit file changes |
| `systemd.tmpfiles.settings` | Create dirs/files/permissions without an activation script |
| `serviceConfig.ExecStartPre` | Prep work bound to the service that needs it |
| `sysinit-reactivation.target` | Re-run oneshots on every activation (switch), not only cold boot |
| `switch-to-configuration` (26.05+) | Reloads (not restarts) when the only unit change is `ExecReload=` |

Two timelines, one desk:

1. **Now (26.05):** stop using the activation restart/reload lists. Prefer unit options and systemd-native prep.
2. **Soon (multi-release):** shrink `system.activationScripts` itself — same migration ladder as the wiki: **tmpfiles → ExecStartPre → dedicated oneshot**.

## Worked examples

### Case 1: Find legacy restart/reload side channels on the desk

On a NixOS 26.05 host (or a flake eval against 26.05), hunt for the deprecated pattern before you bump toward 26.11:

```bash
# Search the desk flake / config tree
rg -n 'activation-restart-list|activation-reload-list|dry-activation-restart-list|dry-activation-reload-list' .
rg -n 'system\.activationScripts' --glob '*.nix' .
```

Representative hit (anti-pattern — do not keep):

```nix
# legacy_restart_from_activation.nix  — remove before 26.11
{ pkgs, ... }:

{
  system.activationScripts.deskTicketReload = ''
    # Ask switch-to-configuration to restart a unit after activation.
    # DEPRECATED in 26.05; REMOVED in 26.11.
    if [ -d /run/nixos ]; then
      echo "desk-ticket.service" >> /run/nixos/activation-restart-list
    fi
  '';
}
```

Also inspect whether anything still echoes reload lists:

```bash
# After a dry run on a lab VM that still has the legacy fragment
sudo nixos-rebuild dry-activate --flake .#desk-workstation
# If present (legacy only):
sudo cat /run/nixos/dry-activation-restart-list 2>/dev/null || true
sudo cat /run/nixos/dry-activation-reload-list 2>/dev/null || true
```

Empty files / missing paths after migration are success. Treat any remaining echo into those lists as a 26.11 blocker ticket.

### Case 2: Restart when a config file changes — use `restartTriggers`

Desk microservice whose unit should restart when its generated config store path changes. Save as `desk_ticket_restart.nix`:

```nix
# desk_ticket_restart.nix
{ config, pkgs, lib, ... }:

let
  ticketConf = pkgs.writeText "desk-ticket.conf" ''
    listen = 127.0.0.1:9471
    desk = family-lab
  '';
in
{
  systemd.services.desk-ticket = {
    description = "Desk ticket stub API";
    wantedBy = [ "multi-user.target" ];
    after = [ "network.target" ];

    # When the store path of ticketConf changes, STC restarts this unit.
    # No activation-script side channel required.
    restartTriggers = [ ticketConf ];

    serviceConfig = {
      Type = "simple";
      ExecStart = "${pkgs.python3}/bin/python3 -m http.server 9471 --bind 127.0.0.1";
      # Real desks pin WorkingDirectory / a real binary; stub keeps the lab cheap.
    };
  };

  # Ship the file somewhere inspectable (optional for the stub).
  environment.etc."desk-ticket/desk-ticket.conf".source = ticketConf;
}
```

Apply and verify the trigger is wired:

```bash
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#desk-workstation
systemctl show desk-ticket.service -p FragmentPath -p DropInPaths
# Bump the conf contents → rebuild → expect a restart of desk-ticket.service
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#desk-workstation
systemctl status desk-ticket.service --no-pager
```

Representative status after a conf-triggered restart:

```
● desk-ticket.service - Desk ticket stub API
     Loaded: loaded (/etc/systemd/system/desk-ticket.service; enabled)
     Active: active (running) since …
```

`restartTriggers` is the boring replacement for "activation script noticed a file moved, please restart unit X."

### Case 3: Prefer reload when only `ExecReload=` changed

NixOS 26.05 also tightened switch-to-configuration itself: when the **only** change to a unit is `ExecReload=`, STC **reloads** instead of restarting; removing `ExecReload=` alone no longer forces a restart. Declare reload-friendly units explicitly:

```nix
# desk_proxy_reload.nix
{ pkgs, ... }:

{
  systemd.services.desk-proxy = {
    description = "Desk reverse-proxy stub";
    wantedBy = [ "multi-user.target" ];
    reloadIfChanged = true;

    serviceConfig = {
      Type = "simple";
      ExecStart = "${pkgs.nginx}/bin/nginx -g 'daemon off;' -c /etc/desk-proxy/nginx.conf";
      ExecReload = "${pkgs.nginx}/bin/nginx -s reload";
      # Keep a minimal conf out of band or via environment.etc — lab sketch only.
    };
  };
}
```

Operator check after editing only the reload command (or a drop-in that only touches `ExecReload=`):

```bash
sudo nixos-rebuild dry-activate --flake .#desk-workstation
# Expect reload planning for desk-proxy, not a full stop/start, when that is the sole diff.
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#desk-workstation
journalctl -u desk-proxy.service -n 20 --no-pager
```

Do not paper over "I need a restart" by writing the unit name into an activation reload list. Set `reloadIfChanged` / `restartTriggers` / `restartIfChanged` on the service.

### Case 4: Replace "mkdir + chown" activation with tmpfiles

Classic activation fragment that only prepares directories:

```nix
# legacy_cache_dir.nix  — anti-pattern
{
  system.activationScripts.deskCache = ''
    mkdir -p /var/cache/desk-ticket
    chown desk-ticket:desk-ticket /var/cache/desk-ticket
    chmod 0750 /var/cache/desk-ticket
  '';
}
```

Boring replacement (`desk_cache_tmpfiles.nix`):

```nix
# desk_cache_tmpfiles.nix
{
  users.users.desk-ticket = {
    isSystemUser = true;
    group = "desk-ticket";
  };
  users.groups.desk-ticket = { };

  systemd.tmpfiles.settings."desk-ticket" = {
    "/var/cache/desk-ticket".d = {
      mode = "0750";
      user = "desk-ticket";
      group = "desk-ticket";
    };
  };
}
```

Verify:

```bash
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#desk-workstation
systemd-tmpfiles --cat-config | rg desk-ticket
ls -ld /var/cache/desk-ticket
```

Representative listing:

```
drwxr-x--- 2 desk-ticket desk-ticket 4096 … /var/cache/desk-ticket
```

### Case 5: Prep that belongs to one service → `ExecStartPre=`

When the script only exists so `some-service` can start cleanly, attach it to that service:

```nix
# desk_ticket_prestart.nix
{ pkgs, ... }:

let
  seed = pkgs.writeShellApplication {
    name = "desk-ticket-seed";
    runtimeInputs = [ pkgs.coreutils ];
    text = ''
      set -euo pipefail
      install -d -m 0750 /var/lib/desk-ticket
      if [ ! -f /var/lib/desk-ticket/seeded ]; then
        date -u +"seeded at %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" > /var/lib/desk-ticket/seeded
      fi
    '';
  };
in
{
  systemd.services.desk-ticket = {
    description = "Desk ticket stub with seed preStart";
    wantedBy = [ "multi-user.target" ];
    serviceConfig = {
      Type = "simple";
      ExecStartPre = [ "${seed}/bin/desk-ticket-seed" ];
      ExecStart = "${pkgs.python3}/bin/python3 -m http.server 9471 --bind 127.0.0.1";
      StateDirectory = "desk-ticket";  # prefer this when a plain state dir is enough
    };
  };
}
```

Prefer `StateDirectory=` / `CacheDirectory=` / `RuntimeDirectory=` when they already express the prep. Use `ExecStartPre=` for custom seed logic that still must run immediately before that unit.

### Case 6: Work that must re-run on every switch → oneshot + `sysinit-reactivation.target`

Activation scripts run on boot **and** on `nixos-rebuild switch`. A oneshot wanted only by `multi-user.target` runs on boot, not necessarily again on every activation. For "run again after each switch," pull in `sysinit-reactivation.target` (desk pattern from current NixOS practice):

```nix
# desk_sync_oneshot.nix
{ pkgs, ... }:

{
  systemd.services.desk-lab-sync = {
    description = "Re-sync desk lab marker on every activation";
    wantedBy = [ "sysinit-reactivation.target" ];
    after = [ "local-fs.target" ];
    path = [ pkgs.coreutils ];

    serviceConfig = {
      Type = "oneshot";
      RemainAfterExit = true;
    };

    script = ''
      set -euo pipefail
      mkdir -p /var/lib/desk-lab
      date -u +"activated %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" >> /var/lib/desk-lab/activations.log
    '';
  };
}
```

Exercise:

```bash
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#desk-workstation
systemctl status desk-lab-sync.service --no-pager
wc -l /var/lib/desk-lab/activations.log
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#desk-workstation
wc -l /var/lib/desk-lab/activations.log   # expect +1 line
```

Representative log growth:

```
1 /var/lib/desk-lab/activations.log
2 /var/lib/desk-lab/activations.log
```

Order relative to user/group managers when needed (`after = [ "userborn.service" ];` or the equivalent on your pin) instead of inventing `activationScripts.*.deps` strings.

## The trap

**Trap A — keep echoing into `/run/nixos/activation-restart-list` "until 26.11."** The list is already deprecated on 26.05; waiting until the removal release is how you get a surprise outage during an otherwise calm channel bump. Migrate on 26.05 while the old path still warns instead of fails.

**Trap B — replace every activation fragment with a oneshot, skipping tmpfiles and `ExecStartPre=`.** You pad the unit graph without gaining clarity. Follow the wiki ladder: **tmpfiles → ExecStartPre → dedicated service**.

**Trap C — assume a oneshot `wantedBy = [ "multi-user.target" ]` re-runs on every `nixos-rebuild switch`.** Cold boot ≠ activation. Use `sysinit-reactivation.target` when you need switch-time re-entry.

**Trap D — disable `reloadIfChanged` / ignore STC's smarter reload behavior, then force restarts via activation lists "to be safe."** Prefer declarative reload/restart metadata on the unit. Let 26.05 STC reload when only `ExecReload=` changed.

```nix
# Anti-pattern — side-channel restart
{
  system.activationScripts.forceNginx = ''
    echo "nginx.service" >> /run/nixos/activation-restart-list
  '';
}
```

```nix
# Boring fix — declare it on the unit
{
  systemd.services.nginx = {
    reloadIfChanged = true;
    restartTriggers = [ /* conf store paths */ ];
  };
}
```

## The boring rule

- On NixOS **26.05**, treat activation-script **reload/restart lists** as deprecated; plan for **removal in 26.11**.
- Never add new `echo … >> /run/nixos/activation-*-list` fragments. Grep the desk flake and delete what you find.
- Express "restart when X changes" with `restartTriggers` / `reloadIfChanged` / `restartIfChanged` on the systemd service.
- Migrate other activation work in order: **`systemd.tmpfiles.settings` → `ExecStartPre=` → oneshot service**.
- For "run again on every switch," use a oneshot `wantedBy = [ "sysinit-reactivation.target" ]`, not a new activation script.
- Expect STC on 26.05 to **reload** (not restart) when the only unit change is `ExecReload=`.
- Track the broader activation-script deprecation (nixpkgs tracking + wiki); this chapter is the reload/restart cut that lands first.

## Try this

1. On a disposable 26.05 VM flake, `rg` for `activation-restart-list`, `activation-reload-list`, and `system.activationScripts`. File a ticket for every out-of-tree hit.
2. Import Case 2's `desk_ticket_restart.nix`, switch, change the conf string, switch again, and confirm `desk-ticket.service` restarted via `journalctl -u desk-ticket`.
3. Convert one real `mkdir`/`chown` activation fragment on the lab host to `systemd.tmpfiles.settings` (Case 4). Diff `ls -ld` before/after.
4. Add Case 6's oneshot, run `nixos-rebuild switch` twice, and confirm `/var/lib/desk-lab/activations.log` gains a line each time.
5. Skim the [Replacing activationScripts](https://wiki.nixos.org/wiki/Replacing_activationScripts) wiki page and the 26.05 release-notes bullet; paste the three-step ladder into the desk runbook.
